codex_why: The high priest calls Jesus “the Son of the Blessed,” and Jesus affirms this identification in MRK 14:62.
judge_why: MRK 14:61 'ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Εὐλογητοῦ' is a claim that Jesus is a son of God, and the owner has ruled that no one is recorded as a son of God/YHVH.

codex_why: The Greek addresses Jesus as Υἱὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου, Son of the Most High God.
judge_why: MRK 5:7 'Υἱὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου' is a son-of-God claim, which the owner has ruled is not recorded.

codex_why: Jesus explicitly calls Zaccheus υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ, a son of Abraham.
judge_why: In LUK 19:9, 'υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ' describes Zacchaeus as a member of Abraham's line or covenant people, not as Abraham's literal son. son-of is the wrong relation type.

codex_why: Jesus explicitly refers to God as “my Father” (τοῦ Πατρός μου).
judge_why: MAT 20:23 'τοῦ Πατρός μου' would be recorded as YHVH father-of Jesus, which is the reverse of son-of-God. The owner's ruling excludes it.

codex_why: The Greek identifies Levi as τὸν τοῦ Ἀλφαίου, meaning the son of Alphaeus.
judge_why: MRK 2:14 does say 'Λευεὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἀλφαίου', but the alphaeus record is described as the father of James (MAT 10:3). The text does not establish that James's father and Levi's father are the same man, and the Gospels never call Levi and James brothers.

codex_why: Jesus calls God «ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος», meaning “my heavenly Father.”
judge_why: MAT 15:13 'ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος' is the son-of-God relation in reverse, which the owner has ruled is not recorded.

codex_why: The Greek calls Jesus Christ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Πατρός, the Son of the Father, identified in the verse as God.
judge_why: 2JN 1:3 'τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Πατρός' is a son-of-God claim, which the owner's ruling excludes.

codex_why: Melchizedek is likened to the Son of God, whom the chapter identifies as Jesus.
judge_why: HEB 7:3 'τῷ Υἱῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ' is a son-of-God claim, which the owner's ruling excludes. The verse also only compares Melchizedek to the Son of God.
